note: Whole-account single-name exposure, across real holdings and open proposals, on one fund running three managers. Illustrative weights. ⚠️ A `proposals` row states the weight that proposal asks the position to *become* — the host's total, not an addition (#813) — so exposure to a name is the larger of the holding and the pending total.

scenarios.name: open-proposals-count-before-they-fill
scenarios.why: Another manager's unfilled proposal is exposure this book has already committed to; counting it only after a fill is how a book ends up at the limit twice in one afternoon. The row states a total of 0.2 — where that manager wants the position to end — so the account's exposure is 0.2 and the ceiling is exactly met.

scenarios.name: per-strategy-caps-do-not-sum-into-a-larger-account-limit
scenarios.why: Three managers each allowed 0.12 of one name is not 0.36 of it. The sum is reported as its own finding, because the way that mistake reaches a book is that nobody adds the three numbers up.

scenarios.name: a-proposal-restates-its-own-strategys-holding
scenarios.why: A trim from 0.14 to 0.08 is a target state, not a purchase of 0.08 on top: summing the two would refuse the trim as a breach. And the trim does not reduce the exposure before it fills — the book holds 0.14 right now — so the fold is `max` and the answer is 0.14 rather than either 0.22 or 0.08 (#813).

scenarios.name: one-name-under-two-theses-is-still-one-position
scenarios.why: ⚠️ This scenario's name said #256's sentence and its arithmetic said the reverse: 0.15 + 0.09 = 0.24, a breach of a 0.2 ceiling on a book holding 0.15. Two position rows for one symbol are a restatement of one quantity — the host merges the rows of an asset into one Position before this package sees them — so the fold is `max`, the position is 0.15, and there is no breach to report. Attribution still splits it: 0.09 is this desk's and 0.06 is not.

scenarios.name: duplicate-rows-still-breach-when-the-one-position-does
scenarios.why: The fold is not a way out of a ceiling. Once the duplicate rows are read as the one position they are, that position is 0.24 against a 0.2 limit and it is a breach — the same answer the sum used to give here for the wrong reason.

scenarios.name: duplicate-rows-under-one-thesis-are-one-position-too
scenarios.why: The same rule where both rows carry this desk's own name. Two 0.06 rows are a 0.06 position, all of it this desk's, and not a 0.12 one — a sum here would refuse this desk's own next rung against exposure the account does not have.
